acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p stoa-transit -- parse_rnews_ passes; all 6 test cases green; clippy clean
description:
What: Implement parse_rnews_batch() — parse a #! rnews batch (possibly compressed) into a Vec of raw article byte vectors.
File: crates/transit/src/import/rnews.rs
Algorithm:
pub fn parse_rnews_batch(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, RnewsError>:
1. Check first 12 bytes for compression markers:
   - b"#! gunbatch" -> call decompress_gunbatch(&input[12..]) (skip the header line including \n), then call parse_rnews_batch recursively on the decompressed bytes
     Wait — the header line is b"#! gunbatch\n" = 12 bytes. Skip to byte 12 for the gzip payload.
   - b"#! cunbatch" -> call decompress_cunbatch(&input[12..]), propagate error or recurse
   - Otherwise: proceed with plain #! rnews parsing
2. Nested compression check: use a depth parameter (default 0); if depth > 0 and a #! g/cunbatch is found, return Err(MalformedBatch("nested compression not supported"))
3. Plain parsing loop:
   a. pos = 0
   b. Loop:
      - Find the end of the next line: scan for \n starting at pos
      - If no \n found and pos < input.len(): return Err(MalformedBatch("unexpected EOF in header line"))
      - Extract line bytes (without \n)
      - If line starts with b"#! rnews ": parse byte count as u64 from &line[9..]
        - If parse fails: Err(MalformedBatch("invalid byte count: {line}"))
        - If count > MAX_ARTICLE_BYTES as u64: Err(MalformedBatch("article exceeds MAX_ARTICLE_BYTES"))
        - let article_start = pos;  let article_end = article_start + count as usize;
        - If article_end > input.len(): Err(MalformedBatch("truncated: declared {count} bytes but only {} remain"))
        - Push input[article_start..article_end].to_vec() to results
        - articles.len() check: if articles.len() > MAX_BATCH_ARTICLES: Err(BatchTooLarge { count: articles.len(), limit: MAX_BATCH_ARTICLES })
        - pos = article_end
      - If pos >= input.len(): break
   c. Return Ok(articles)

Implementation detail: The #! gunbatch / #! cunbatch check must look at the FIRST LINE only. Check if input starts with b"#! gunbatch\n" (12 bytes) or b"#! cunbatch\n" (12 bytes). Use starts_with for this check.

Defensive rules:
- All byte count arithmetic uses checked ops or explicit bounds checks before any slice indexing
- Never unwrap — all parse failures return RnewsError
- article_start and article_end must both be <= input.len() before slicing
- The inner recursive call for compressed batches passes depth+1

Tests (in same file, #[cfg(test)]):
- parse_batch_two_articles:
  Oracle: hand-computed bytes of two known articles
  Input: construct b"#! rnews 163\nFrom: alice@example.com\n...163 bytes...#! rnews 161\n...161 bytes..."
  Assert: result has 2 articles; first article bytes == known article 1; second == known article 2
- parse_batch_empty_input: parse_rnews_batch(b"") == Ok(vec![])
- parse_batch_count_cap: 1001 articles of 1 byte each → Err(BatchTooLarge { count: 1001, limit: 1000 })
- parse_batch_malformed_no_count: b"#! rnews\n" → Err(MalformedBatch(_))
- parse_batch_truncated: declare n=100 but only 50 bytes follow → Err(MalformedBatch(_))
- parse_batch_count_too_large: #! rnews with count > MAX_ARTICLE_BYTES → Err(MalformedBatch(_))
title: parse_rnews_batch: #! rnews batch format parser
